description: REQ-114's own stated purpose is to close a specific 'bust-out/reputation-laundering' pattern: 'a borrower ... can therefore cheaply build a strong track record via a sequence of small, low-risk, successfully-repaid cold-start-tier loans, then strategically default on the SINGLE largest loan its now-inflated reputation qualifies it for from a DIFFERENT, unsuspecting lender' (behavioral-spec.md:812-816), closed by making the monitor DOLLAR-weighted rather than count-weighted so 'a single large default's own dollar weight is NOT diluted by loan COUNT' (:892-895). This protects correctly against dilution by loan COUNT (many small loans alongside one big default). It does NOT protect against, and never mentions, dilution by loan VOLUME: once `sampleSize >= 10`, `evaluateOverallDefaultKillSwitch` pauses only when `defaultRateUsd > 0.20`, and `defaultRateUsd = totalDefaultedUsd / totalIssuedUsd` is computed over the SUM of ALL terminal loans' principal, including any OTHER, unrelated, HEALTHY established-tier (`$0.04`-`$5.00`) loans that happened to also reach a terminal 'repaid' state. Concretely: a colony with 10 large ($5.00) established-tier loans, 9 healthy repayments ($45 total) plus exactly the bust-out pattern's own single $5.00 default, yields `totalIssuedUsd=$50`, `totalDefaultedUsd=$5.00`, `defaultRateUsd=0.10` -- BELOW the `0.20` threshold, so `paused:false`. The EXACT scenario REQ-114 was written to catch (an established borrower defaulting on its single largest loan) is silently masked below threshold the moment a colony has accumulated enough OTHER, unrelated, legitimately-large loan volume -- which is precisely the state a maturing colony (the whole point of REQ-105's doubling ladder) will eventually reach. The requirement's own Edge Cases section (behavioral-spec.md:878-905) discusses dilution-by-loan-COUNT twice (once for `sampleSize<10`, once contrasting count-based vs dollar-based ratios) but never discusses, flags, or accepts this DIFFERENT dilution-by-loan-VOLUME failure mode once `sampleSize>=10` -- an asymmetry this document does not disclose anywhere, unlike its own careful, explicit-limitation discipline elsewhere in this SAME document (`GOJO_SENDER_ID`'s single-sender assumption, the reconciled-path `issued_ms` asymmetry, the `borrower_`-prefix lock-key collision risk, and the `0.20` threshold's own 'unvalidated placeholder' flag at :862-876 -- which flags only the NUMBER as unvalidated, not this specific structural blind spot in what the number can ever detect once the colony scales past the small-sample regime).

evidence.snippet: Many small, healthy, cold-start-tier loans are repaid on time (a large `totalIssuedUsd` denominator from MANY small numerators) alongside ONE large established-tier default: because `totalIssuedUsd`/`totalDefaultedUsd` are DOLLAR sums (never loan counts), the single large default's own dollar weight is NOT diluted by loan COUNT the way a naive 'defaulted loans / total loans' count-based ratio would dilute it -- a `$5.00` default among ninety-nine `$0.02` repayments is still a meaningfully large fraction of total dollar volume at risk, not `1/100`.

crossCheck.note: PROP-114a/b's own worked fixture (8 small `$0.02` loans + 1 `$5.00` default -> defaultRateUsd~=0.969, paused:true) only demonstrates the count-dilution case is closed. No PROP anywhere in the 149-row table constructs a fixture with MULTIPLE other large ($0.04-$5.00), HEALTHY, terminal loans coexisting with a single large default to check whether `defaultRateUsd` can fall below `0.20` in exactly the scenario REQ-114's own rationale (:807-821) describes as the pattern it exists to close.
